_instructions.howToUse: This is the portfolio source-of-truth. Populate the portfolio UI from this file. Do not invent missing facts.
rules: Use the content in this file as the primary portfolio source.
Do not invent metrics, users, revenue, downloads, performance percentages, business outcomes or production claims.
Public live URLs are production proof. Internal company products keep liveUrl null and must be labeled as not publicly available.
Do not use Lead titles unless people leadership is true. Use Frontend Product Engineer as the public role title.
Leave teamSize null unless an exact product-team count is known. Do not set teamSize to 1 for frontend-only ownership — backend is typically a separate team. Do not invent team sizes or metrics.
Frontend and UI/UX may be described as sole or primary ownership. Do not claim sole engineer for the whole product when backend is handled by others.
Do not claim a shared reusable payment layer across products. Stripe and Razorpay were implemented as product-specific payment flows.
Use first-person ownership language only where the project evidence supports it.
Keep project-level functionality separate from personal ownership.
Production applications may have detailed case studies.
Mobile applications may have detailed case studies. Do not claim app-store publication unless a live store URL exists.
Internal tools and prototypes may have detailed case studies; keep them distinct from production products.
Business websites remain card-based portfolio items with live URLs rather than deep product case studies.
Do not expose private API keys, Firebase credentials, secrets, client credentials or confidential information.
Use empty strings or empty arrays when information is genuinely unavailable.
featured should be true only for the strongest flagship production projects.
priority controls display order within each category.
frame must be product, systems or delivery.
archiveCategory must be production, websites, mobile or internal-tools.

productionApplications.name: ProCoach
productionApplications.statusDetail: Production-intended product UI with real API and payment integrations
productionApplications.oneLiner: A two-sided coaching marketplace where coaches publish paid sessions and learners discover, enroll, and pay in one product.
productionApplications.description: ProCoach connects sports and fitness coaches with learners through session discovery, scheduling, enrollment, and payments. The product serves coaches, learners, and parents enrolling children — each with role-specific workflows inside one authenticated web application.
productionApplications.overview: The product brings the operational side of coaching sessions and the learner booking experience into one authenticated web application. Coaches can create and manage sessions, invite participants, handle enrollment operations and manage payouts, while learners can discover sessions, enroll themselves or children, complete payments and manage their account.
productionApplications.problem: Coaches needed a product for publishing and operating paid sessions, while learners and parents needed a reliable way to discover sessions, enroll and pay. The frontend also had to coordinate multiple APIs, authentication states, session workflows and payment flows while being delivered as a statically hosted Next.js application.
productionApplications.solution: Built and evolved the frontend product experience around role-specific workflows, reusable feature structures, API integrations and embedded Stripe payment experiences. The application connects profile, schedules and payment services into the coach and learner journeys.
productionApplications.role: Frontend Product Engineer on the ProCoach web client — product UI, UI/UX, and feature workflows. I owned frontend and UI/UX; backend was handled separately, and I contribute there when needed.
productionApplications.backendContribution: Integrated and orchestrated existing backend services from the frontend. No backend service ownership is claimed from this repository.
ownership: Majority of UI feature delivery represented in the available Git history.
Coach session creation and management surfaces.
SMS consent and authentication-related frontend flows.
Coach overview and related dashboard integration.
Frontend integration with profile, schedules and payments APIs.
Stripe Embedded Checkout integration on the client.
Frontend handling of payment confirmation and retry behaviour.
features: Draft, scheduled and historical session workflows

database: Backend-managed persistence; no database layer in frontend repository

engineeringChallenges.title: Reliable paid enrollment
engineeringChallenges.description: Enrollment could involve the schedules API, payments API and Stripe succeeding at different stages. The frontend therefore had to manage the transition from enrollment review to checkout and then payment confirmation/retry rather than treating payment as a single UI action.

engineeringChallenges.title: Static hosting with dynamic product workflows
engineeringChallenges.description: The application was designed as a static Next.js export while still supporting dynamic session and enrollment URLs. Routing and fallback behaviour therefore had to work within the static hosting model.

engineeringChallenges.title: Multiple API services
engineeringChallenges.description: The frontend consumes separate services for authentication/profile, schedules and payments, requiring a consistent client-side integration layer and session handling.

engineeringChallenges.title: Timezone-sensitive session information
engineeringChallenges.description: Session dates and times need to remain meaningful across user-facing scheduling and calendar views, requiring deliberate date parsing and formatting.

engineeringChallenges.title: Deep-linked authenticated workflows
engineeringChallenges.description: Users can enter product flows from links and invitations, so the frontend has to carry the intended destination through authentication and onboarding.

architectureDecisions: Static Next.js export for the frontend deployment model.
Feature-oriented hooks and view structures for product workflows.
React Context for selected cross-cutting application state.
Client-side authentication because the deployment model has no server runtime.
Embedded Stripe experiences rather than building a custom card-entry flow.
Dedicated frontend API client behaviour for multiple service origins.
Client-side session expiry handling.
impact: Delivered a substantial production-shaped frontend for a two-sided coaching marketplace.
Connected real product workflows across authentication, sessions, enrollment and payments.
Implemented a real payment experience rather than a static checkout mock.
Created distinct coach and learner experiences around the same product.

caseStudy.heroTitle: Coaching marketplace — from session to payment
caseStudy.heroSubtitle: Building the frontend that connects coaches, learners, and Stripe across multiple production APIs.
caseStudy.context: ProCoach is a sports and fitness coaching marketplace. Coaches need to publish sessions, manage enrollments, and handle payouts. Learners and parents need a reliable path to discover sessions, enroll, and pay. I owned the web client that ties these journeys together.
caseStudy.problem: The product had to support the full coaching workflow — session publishing, enrollment, payments, and payouts — while coordinating several backend services from a statically hosted Next.js frontend.
caseStudy.approach: I treated the frontend as the product layer: not isolated screens, but connected workflows from discovery through enrollment, checkout, confirmation, and retry states.
technicalImplementation: Next.js App Router with static export
REST API integration across multiple service domains
Client-side payment confirmation and retry handling
engineeringDecisions: Static hosting shaped routing and authentication architecture.
Payment was implemented as a stateful product workflow rather than a standalone checkout screen.
Feature-specific state was kept close to the workflow instead of introducing a large global state library.
caseStudy.production: The repository contains production-oriented configuration, multiple API environments, Stripe integrations, CSP handling and static deployment configuration. Exact live traffic and business metrics are not established by the repository.
caseStudy.outcome: A production-shaped marketplace frontend connecting real coaching, enrollment, and payment workflows — without claiming unverified business metrics.

portfolioPresentation.homepageSummary: Two-sided coaching marketplace with real session, enrollment and payment workflows.
portfolioPresentation.workPageSummary: Marketplace frontend spanning coach operations, learner booking, and Stripe payments.

productionApplications.name: KhetiValah
productionApplications.statusDetail: Production web application — marketplace, booking, and payment workflows
productionApplications.oneLiner: Agricultural marketplace and event booking on the web — listings, stall booking, Razorpay payments, and GST billing across vendor, sponsor, and participant roles.
productionApplications.description: KhetiValah is a production web platform for agricultural commerce and event participation. Vendors, sponsors, farmers, buyers, and participants use role-specific workflows for listings, stall booking, registrations, product catalogs, checkout, and billing.
productionApplications.overview: The web application connects marketplace discovery, event stall booking, sponsorship plans, participant registration, vendor product management, and payment operations in one multi-role product.
productionApplications.problem: Agricultural participants need more than static listings. Vendors must book stalls and manage products, sponsors select plans, attendees register and pay, and every role needs reliable Razorpay checkout, billing, and order visibility on the web.
productionApplications.solution: A React web client integrated with the AgriEvents / marketplace backend — role-aware booking flows, Razorpay payment UI, GST billing surfaces, catalog management, and operational dashboards.
productionApplications.role: Frontend Product Engineer on the KhetiValah web application — marketplace UI, booking flows, payments, and API integration. Primary frontend and UI/UX engineer, with other developers also involved. Backend was handled separately; I contribute there when needed.
productionApplications.backendContribution: Frontend integration with Spring Boot / AgriEvents REST APIs. Backend service ownership is not claimed.
ownership: Marketplace and event discovery interfaces on the web.
Razorpay payment UI and payment-state handling.
Vendor product catalog and listing management.
Early Bird Offers and Stand Types modules.
OTP authentication and account flows on the web.
Operational dashboards and order/payment history views.
REST API integration across marketplace and event services.
features: Farmer, buyer, investor, and vendor workflows
Event discovery and event detail pages

engineeringChallenges.title: Multi-role booking and checkout
engineeringChallenges.description: Vendors, sponsors, and participants follow different booking paths, but all converge on shared payment, billing, and order visibility requirements.

engineeringChallenges.title: Razorpay and billing together
engineeringChallenges.description: Payment success, GST-related billing, and order state had to stay aligned across the UI and multiple backend responses.

engineeringChallenges.title: Marketplace data on the web
engineeringChallenges.description: Listings, availability, early-bird offers, and stand types required transforming API-shaped data into usable booking and catalog interfaces.

engineeringChallenges.title: Booking reconciliation
engineeringChallenges.description: Returning users needed previously selected stalls and order lines reflected accurately when they resumed a booking flow.

architectureDecisions: Web-first product architecture with role-aware routes and modules.
Service layer around shared REST API integration.
Separate booking, catalog, and payment UI flows instead of one generic form.
Environment-based API configuration for staging and production.
Payment treated as a stateful workflow, not a single checkout button.
impact: Delivered production web workflows for marketplace discovery, booking, and payments.
Connected Razorpay and GST billing into real participant and vendor journeys.
Supported multiple agricultural roles inside one web product.

caseStudy.heroTitle: Agriculture marketplace — booking and payments on the web
caseStudy.heroSubtitle: Listings, stall booking, Razorpay checkout, and GST billing for vendors, sponsors, and participants.
caseStudy.context: KhetiValah on the web is the production platform for agricultural marketplace and event participation. Mobile is a separate client — this case study covers the web application.
caseStudy.problem: The business needed a web product where different roles could book, register, pay, and manage catalogs — with Razorpay and billing treated as part of the real workflow, not an afterthought.
caseStudy.approach: I built the web client around the business journeys that actually generate revenue and participation — discovery, booking, payment, billing, and post-payment visibility.
technicalImplementation: REST API integration with marketplace and event services
Razorpay payment UI and status handling
Catalog, Early Bird Offers, and Stand Types modules
engineeringDecisions: Keep booking, payments, and billing as connected workflows.
Use a shared API layer across marketplace and event modules.
Present role-specific UI without duplicating the entire application.
caseStudy.production: Production web application with real payment and booking integrations. Mobile companion app is documented separately under Khetivala App.
caseStudy.outcome: A production web platform connecting agricultural marketplace discovery, booking, Razorpay payments, and billing workflows.

portfolioPresentation.homepageSummary: Agricultural web marketplace with booking, Razorpay, and GST billing.
portfolioPresentation.workPageSummary: Production web platform for marketplace discovery, stall booking, and payments.

productionApplications.name: RDR Tech
productionApplications.statusDetail: Production web application for internal company use — not publicly available.
productionApplications.oneLiner: Real-time workflow platform for audit and tax teams — task management, live dashboards, role-based workflows, and WebSocket-driven updates on the web.

productionApplications.overview: The web product replaces fragmented coordination with structured workflows, operational dashboards, and live status updates across roles in an audit and compliance practice.
productionApplications.problem: Audit and tax teams need shared visibility into tasks, workload, and workflow state. Static dashboards and manual refresh are not enough when multiple users act on the same operational data.
productionApplications.solution: A React web client with WebSocket-driven updates, role-aware workflow transitions, dense operational dashboards, and REST API integration with a Node.js backend.
productionApplications.role: Frontend Product Engineer on the RDR Tech web client — workflow UI, dashboards, real-time state, and API integration. I owned frontend and UI/UX; backend was handled separately, and I contribute there when needed.
productionApplications.backendContribution: Worked with the Node.js backend and real-time event lifecycle; backend service ownership is not claimed from the frontend repository.

Subscription and billing-related UI where applicable.
REST API integration and client-side state handling.
Production maintenance on the web client.

engineeringChallenges.title: Role-aware workflow states

engineeringChallenges.title: Dense operational dashboards

engineeringChallenges.title: Concurrent updates

WebSockets for live workflow synchronization instead of polling.
Role-aware UI composition around workflow states.
Reusable dashboard and table patterns for operational data.
Frontend structured around workflow modules rather than isolated pages.
